_comment: WS4 BCC coarse sweep (user spec, 2026-06). Grid: M x S x centerM x node_mass_amplitude on the bcc node geometry at default n_shells=2 = 386 external nodes (a volume-filling lattice, ~15x cube26's 26 nodes -> heavier tidal calc per step). 2000 inner particles, so every cell is N>=1000 -> Barnes-Hut self-gravity throughout (one consistent force method, no switch). centerM = outer-mass multiplier (N_total = centerM * particle_count). centerM limited to [1,2] for this first coarse pass (we go from there). amp = per-node HMEA mass anisotropy (mean-preserving; amp=0 collapses to one nm_seed). Objective: minimize chi2/dof vs real Pantheon+; chi2_lcdm~0.436 / chi2_eds~0.843 are reference benchmarks only. init_distribution=uniform_sphere (NOT grf). NOTE: probe_timing in sweep.py hardcodes cube26 for its s/sim estimate, so the printed ETA UNDER-estimates these 386-node bcc cells; judge runtime from the per-cell times in the log.
